sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领导人，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·莫达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上免费向所有人直播精选访谈。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the president holds an extraordinary news conference to address, for a third time, the violence in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 今天，总统举行了一场非同寻常的新闻发布会，第三次就夏洛茨维尔的暴力事件发表讲话。

sentences.en: Asked if he equates white supremacists with counter-protesters on the left, the president says, I am not putting anybody on a moral plane.
sentences.zh: 当被问及他是否将白人至上主义者与左翼反抗议者等同视付时，总统说：“我没有把任何人放在道德层面进行衡量。”

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月16日，星期三。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Great to be back in New York with all of our friends.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和我们的所有朋友回到纽约。

sentences.en: Mark Lanner, can you describe the scene for us on Tuesday afternoon?
sentences.zh: 马克·拉纳，你能为我们描述一下周二下午的现场吗？

sentences.en: Well, President Trump was back on his home turf.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特朗普总统回到了他熟悉的地盘。

sentences.en: He was in the lobby of his tower, Trump Tower, in midtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 他在曼哈顿中城他的大楼——特朗普大厦的大堂里。

sentences.en: It's a familiar scene for many of us who covered the transition.
sentences.zh: 对于我们许多报道过过渡期的人来说，这是一个熟悉的场景。

sentences.en: This time it was different because there was a podium with a presidential seal and flags, and he was surrounded by cabinet secretaries.
sentences.zh: 这次不同的是，现场有一个带有总统印章和旗帜的讲台，周围环绕着内阁部长们。

sentences.en: On what we're going to be discussing today, which is infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 关于我们今天要讨论的话题，也就是基础设施。

sentences.en: And he had come to basically talk about a meeting on infrastructure, which is one of his legislative priorities.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是来谈论一次关于基础设施的会议，这是他的立法优先事项之一。

sentences.en: The questions, of course, were mostly about what happened last weekend in Charlottesville,
sentences.zh: 当然，问题主要集中在上周末夏洛茨维尔发生的事情上，

sentences.en: and the president, rather than avoiding the topic, plunged right into it, and the press conference quickly took on a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 而总统非但没有回避这个话题，反而直接切入其中，新闻发布会很快便自行引发了极大的关注。

sentences.en: But unlike you and unlike, excuse me, unlike you and unlike the media, before I make a statement,
sentences.zh: 但不同于你，也不同于，对不起，不同于你，也不同于媒体，在我发表声明之前，

sentences.en: I'd like to know the facts.
sentences.zh: 我想了解事实。

sentences.en: Reporters began asking him to clarify remarks he had made about the violence in Charlottesville last weekend.
sentences.zh: 记者们开始要求他澄清上周末就夏洛茨维尔暴力事件所发表的言论。

sentences.en: One of the first questions came from a colleague of ours, Maggie Haberman, who asked him if what happened in Charlottesville was terrorism.
sentences.zh: 最早的问题之一来自我们的同事玛吉·哈伯曼，她问他夏洛茨维尔发生的事情是否是恐怖主义。

sentences.en: Well, I think the driver of the car is a disgrace to himself, his family, and this country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为开车的那个司机对他自己、他的家庭和这个国家来说都是一种耻辱。

sentences.en: And that is, you can call it terrorism.
sentences.zh: 你可以称之为恐怖主义。

sentences.en: You can call it murder.
sentences.zh: 你可以称之为谋杀。

sentences.en: You can call it whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 你想叫它什么都行。

sentences.en: I would just call it as the fastest one to come up with a good verdict.
sentences.zh: 我只会把它当作最快得出好结论的事情来看待。

sentences.en: That's what I'd call it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的看法。

sentences.en: Because there is a question.
sentences.zh: 因为这里存在一个问题。

sentences.en: Is it murder?
sentences.zh: 这是谋杀吗？

sentences.en: Is it terrorism?
sentences.zh: 这是恐怖主义吗？

sentences.en: And then you get into legal semantics.
sentences.zh: 然后你就陷入了法律语义的争论。

sentences.en: The driver of the car is a murderer.
sentences.zh: 开车的司机是个谋杀犯。

sentences.en: And what he did was a horrible, horrible, inexcusable thing.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是一件可怕的、可怕的、不可原谅的事情。

sentences.en: So, Mark, the president's attorney general has called this quite clearly an act of terrorism, the driving of this car into the crowd.
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，总统的司法部长已经非常明确地将这起汽车冲撞人群的事件称为恐怖主义行径。

sentences.en: The president is not willing to use that word categorically.
sentences.zh: 但总统并不愿意斩钉截铁地使用这个词。

sentences.en: And, of course, the interesting point to make here is that President Trump has been fiercely
sentences.zh: 当然，这里值得指出有趣的一点是，特朗普总统一直以来都在猛烈

sentences.en: critical of other politicians, and particularly President Obama, who refused to use the phrase radical Islamic terrorism.
sentences.zh: 批评其他政治家，尤其是拒绝使用“激进伊斯兰恐怖主义”这一词汇的奥巴马总统。

sentences.en: And yet, in this case, when it involves a domestic and racially inspired case of violence,
sentences.zh: 然而在这种情况下，当涉及国内和带有种族动机的暴力事件时，

sentences.en: it's President Trump who shrinks from using the phrase terrorism, even if, as you point out, his own attorney general is open to calling it that.
sentences.zh: 反而是特朗普总统对使用“恐怖主义”一词退避三舍，哪怕正如你所指出的那样，他自己的司法部长并不排斥这样称呼。

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: And you had some very bad people in that group.
sentences.zh: 那个群体里有一些非常糟糕的人。

sentences.en: But you also had people that were very fine people on both sides.
sentences.zh: 但你们也看到，双方都有非常好的人。

sentences.en: He sort of blurred the distinction where, you know, most people would say that the alt-right, the neo-Nazis, the white nationalists brought an agenda of hate into this situation.
sentences.zh: 他有点模糊了界限，你知道的，大多数人会认为另类右翼、新纳粹分子和白人民族主义者将仇恨的议程带入了这种局势中。

sentences.en: He's trying to muddy the waters a bit and draw this rough equivalence between the two sides.
sentences.zh: 他试图把水搅浑一点，在双方之间划出一个粗略的等号。

sentences.en: So, Mark, then the president introduces a phrase that I hadn't heard before.
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，接着总统抛出了一个我以前没听过的词汇。

sentences.en: What about the alt-left that came charging at the, as you say, the alt-right?
sentences.zh: 那群冲向——正如你所说——另类右翼的另类左翼又该怎么说？

sentences.en: Do they have any semblance of guilt?
sentences.zh: 他们有任何负罪感吗？

sentences.en: The alt-left.
sentences.zh: 另类左翼。

sentences.en: Let me ask you this.
sentences.zh: 让我问你这个。

sentences.en: What about the fact that they came charging, that they came charging with clubs in their hands, swinging clubs?
sentences.zh: 他们冲过来，手里拿着棍棒、挥舞着棍棒冲过来，这件事怎么说？

sentences.en: Do they have any problem?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: I think they do.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们有。

sentences.en: You heard that term before.
sentences.zh: 你以前听过这个词吗？

sentences.en: Is that a term?
sentences.zh: 这是一个词吗？

sentences.en: Horrible day.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的一天。

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: I'm not finished.
sentences.zh: 我还没说完。

sentences.en: I'm not finished, fake news.
sentences.zh: 我还没说完，假新闻。

sentences.en: It's certainly very new.
sentences.zh: 这当然非常新颖。

sentences.en: And I think that it's actually something that is growing out of the aftermath of Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这实际上是夏洛茨维尔事件余波中滋生出来的东西。

sentences.en: I think one of the key drivers on the side of the alt-right in this effort to kind of draw moral equivalence is to brand a very disparate group of people who are counter-protesters under the banner of the alt-left.
sentences.zh: 我认为，另类右翼在这场试图制造某种道德对等的努力中的一个关键推动因素，就是把抗议者这样一个极其杂乱的群体打上“另类左翼”的旗号。

sentences.en: And in a way, it's ironic because the alt-right insists that they are not a sinister force, that they're motivated by love of country and patriotism.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这很具有讽刺意味，因为另类右翼坚称他们不是一股险恶的力量，他们的动机是对国家的爱和爱国主义。

sentences.en: Yet they seem to be eager to use the bad rap that the phrase alt-right has gotten and apply it to this group of counter-protesters and demonstrators.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们似乎又急于把“另类右翼”这个词所获得的坏名声，套在这个反抗议者和示威者群体身上。

sentences.en: I will tell you something.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你一件事。

sentences.en: I watched those very closely, much more closely than you people watched it.
sentences.zh: 我非常仔细地观看了那些画面，比你们这群人看的要仔细得多。

sentences.en: And you have, you had a group on one side that was bad and you had a group on the other side that was also very violent.
sentences.zh: 一边有一个糟糕的群体，而另一边也有一个非常暴力的群体。

sentences.en: And nobody wants to say that, but I'll say it right now.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意这么说，但我现在就要说。

sentences.en: You had a group, you had a group on the other side that came charging in without a permit and they were very, very violent.
sentences.zh: 你们有一个群体，另一边有一个没有许可证就冲进来的群体，他们非常、非常暴力。

sentences.en: I think that the president is picking up on a theme that we're going to be hearing more and more of in the social media on the alt-right.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统捕捉到了一个主题，我们以后会在另类右翼的社交媒体上越来越多地听到这个主题。

sentences.en: And that's, again,
sentences.zh: 那就是，再次，

sentences.en: to somehow suggest that there is a parallel group on the far left that uses tactics that are every bit as rough and are every bit as sinister in their motivation as many think the alt-right is.
sentences.zh: 不知何故暗示在极左翼阵营中存在一个平行群体，他们所使用的战术同样粗暴，其动机也同许多人认为的另类右翼一样险恶。

sentences.en: Do you think that what you call the alt-left is the same as neo-Nazis?
sentences.zh: 你认为你所谓的另类左翼和新纳粹是一样的吗？

sentences.en: I, those people, all of those people, excuse me, I've condemned neo-Nazis.
sentences.zh: 我，那些人，所有那些人，对不起，我已经谴责过新纳粹了。

sentences.en: I've condemned many different groups, but not all of those people were neo-Nazis, believe me.
sentences.zh: 我谴责过许多不同的群体，但相信我，并非所有那些人都是新纳粹。

sentences.en: Not all of those people were white supremacists by any stretch.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，并非所有那些人都是白人至上主义者。

sentences.en: Those people were also there because they wanted to protest the taking down of a statue, Robert E.
sentences.zh: 那些人之所以也在场，是因为他们想抗议拆除罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee.
sentences.zh: 李的雕像。

sentences.en: So, excuse me, and you take a look at some of the groups and you see, and you know it if you were honest reporters, which in many cases you're not.
sentences.zh: 所以，打扰一下，你看看其中的一些群体就会明白，如果你是个诚实的记者——而你在很多情况下并不是——你就会知道。

sentences.en: Right, he seems to be focused on what happened in the park that day, very, very literally.
sentences.zh: 没错，他似乎非常、非常字面地专注于那天在公园里发生的事情。

sentences.en: But he doesn't seem to be putting it all into a larger context of why these two sides were there and what each side represents.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎并没有把这一切放入更大的背景中去考量，即双方为什么会出现在那里，以及每一方代表了什么。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: By focusing on it in such a granular way, he's purposely avoiding the larger context,
sentences.zh: 通过如此细致入微地聚焦于此，他是在刻意回避更大的背景，

sentences.en: which is that these groups came into this progressive university town to a university founded by Thomas Jefferson and tried to use this, you know,
sentences.zh: 也就是这些群体来到这座由托马斯·杰斐逊创立的大学所在的进步大学城，试图利用这个，你知道的，

sentences.en: I don't want to call it hallowed ground because that's probably overstating it, but used a place that's freighted with symbolism to champion and deliver a message of hatred,
sentences.zh: 我不想称之为神圣的土地，因为那可能夸大其词了，但利用一个充满象征意义的地方来宣扬并传达仇恨的信息，

sentences.en: of xenophobia, of whites reclaiming the country.
sentences.zh: 传达仇外心理、白人夺回国家的信息。

sentences.en: And I think that that context is lost when you treat it almost in a dry police blotter way and just focus on who is throwing a punch at whom, which is, I think,
sentences.zh: 而我认为，当你几乎以枯燥的警察记事簿方式来对待它，只关注谁在向谁挥拳时，这种背景就丢失了，我认为，

sentences.en: the way the president was trying to portray it in the news conference.
sentences.zh: 这就是总统在新闻发布会上试图描绘它的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, is purposely avoiding it one take and is potentially another, the idea that the president of the United States, this president,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，刻意回避是一种看法，而另一种可能则是，美国总统，这位总统，

sentences.en: doesn't really see the world that way through context and through history and maybe with as much nuance?
sentences.zh: 其实并不是通过背景、历史以及或许同样多的细微差别来看待这个世界的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think in this case,
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这种情况下，

sentences.en: it also represents a deliberate effort to rob it of that broader context and allow him to make these points about equivalency that are simply not possible to make once you put it into any historical context.
sentences.zh: 这也代表了一种蓄意的努力，剥夺了其更广泛的背景，从而让他能够提出这些关于对等的观点，而一旦你把它置于任何历史背景中，这些观点根本就是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: So, Mark, you mentioned this idea of moral equivalence, and there's a very big moment in this news conference that seems quite memorable beyond this news conference,
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，你提到了这种道德对等的概念，在这场新闻发布会上有一个非常重大的时刻，除了这场新闻发布会本身之外，它似乎令人难忘，

sentences.en: maybe even for the presidency, that's kind of around this idea.
sentences.zh: 甚至对整个总统任期而言也是如此，它正是围绕着这个概念展开的。

sentences.en: Are you putting what you're calling the alt-left and white supremacists on the same moral plane?
sentences.zh: 你把所谓的另类左翼和白人至上主义者放在同一个道德层面上了吗？

sentences.en: I'm not putting anybody on a moral plane.
sentences.zh: 我没有把任何人放在道德层面。

sentences.en: What I'm saying is this.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是：

sentences.en: You had a group on one side and you had a group on the other, and they came at each other with clubs, and it was vicious, and it was horrible, and it was a horrible thing to watch.
sentences.zh: 一边有一个群体，另一边也有一个群体，他们带着棍棒冲向彼此，那是残酷的，那是可怕的，看着这一切令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: And the president's answer was fascinating.
sentences.zh: 总统的回答十分引人入胜。

sentences.en: He said, I'm not putting anybody on a moral plane.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我没有把任何人放在道德层面。”

sentences.en: But there is another side.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一方。

sentences.en: There was a group on this side, you can call them the left, or you've just called them the left, that came violently attacking the other group.
sentences.zh: 这边有一个群体，你可以称他们为左翼，或者你刚刚称他们为左翼，他们对另一群体发动了暴力袭击。

sentences.en: So you can say what you want, but that's the way it is.
sentences.zh: 所以你想怎么说都行，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: On both sides, sir?
sentences.zh: 双方都有责任吗，先生？

sentences.en: You said there was hatred, there was violence on both sides.
sentences.zh: 您说过双方都有仇恨，双方都有暴力。

sentences.en: Well, I do think there's blame, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实认为双方都有责任，是的。

sentences.en: I think there's blame on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我认为双方都有责任。

sentences.en: You look at both sides, I think there's blame on both sides.
sentences.zh: 你看看双方，我认为双方都有责任。

sentences.en: And I have no doubt about it, and you don't have any doubt about it either.
sentences.zh: 对此我毫无疑问，你们也毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And if you reported it accurately, you would say.
sentences.zh: 如果你如实报道，你就会这么说。

sentences.en: And I think this is actually an extremely important moment, perhaps the most telling moment of the news conference, because the president, in effect, was saying,
sentences.zh: 而我认为这实际上是一个极其重要的时刻，也许是这场新闻发布会上最能说明问题的时刻，因为总统实际上是在说，

sentences.en: I'm not here to set down a moral standard.
sentences.zh: 我来这里不是为了确立道德标准的。

sentences.en: This is what presidents do.
sentences.zh: 这就是总统们的职责。

sentences.en: This is what the modern American presidency is about.
sentences.zh: 这就是现代美国总统职责的意义所在。

sentences.en: It's about setting a moral benchmark that the citizenry that Americans can all kind of understand is the standard.
sentences.zh: 它的意义在于树立一个道德标杆，让广大公民、让所有美国人都能够理解这便是标准。

sentences.en: The president is really the only person in American society who has that powerful a role to play.
sentences.zh: 总统确实是美国社会中唯一扮演如此强有力角色的人。

sentences.en: President Trump today said, I'm not interested in doing that.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统今天却说：“我对做这件事不感兴趣。”

sentences.en: That's an abdication of something that's very central to the role of the presidency.
sentences.zh: 这是对总统核心职责的一种抛弃。

sentences.en: And I think it's something that we will be talking about and thinking about the implications of for quite some time.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在相当长的一段时间里，我们都会一直在讨论并思考其带来的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, Mark, I was reminded of something that I went rooting around for when I read that quote, which was from President Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马克，当我读到那句引用自罗斯福总统的话时，让我想起了某些东西。

sentences.en: And he said that the presidency is preeminently a place of moral leadership.
sentences.zh: 他说过，总统职位主要是一个发挥道德领导力的地方。

sentences.en: And I think we can all think of moments in the presidencies of our lifetime where a president was called upon to do that or called upon himself to do that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都能想到在我们有生之年的总统任期内，某个总统被要求这样做，或者主动要求自己这样做的时刻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think in some ways it's the it's the deepest calling of a leader and the most difficult challenge of a leader.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某些方面，这是一位领导者最深层的召唤，也是最具挑战性的考验。

sentences.en: And in my time covering the White House, I watched President Obama wrestle with this on the race issue.
sentences.zh: 在我报道白宫的期间，我看着奥巴马总统在种族问题上与此进行挣扎。

sentences.en: He didn't always summon the words exactly the way he wanted to.
sentences.zh: 他并不总是能完全如愿以偿地找到最恰当的词汇。

sentences.en: But he, I think, viewed it as the greatest test of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 但我想，他将此视为对他总统任期最大的考验。

sentences.en: So to hear President Trump, in effect, say this isn't part of my job description was a stunning moment.
sentences.zh: 因此，听到特朗普总统实际上说这不属于我的工作职责，真是一个令人震惊的时刻。

sentences.en: You had people in that group that were there to protest the taking down of to them a very, very important statue and the renaming of a park from Robert E.
sentences.zh: 那个群体里有些人到场是为了抗议拆除对他们而言非常、非常重要的雕像，以及将一个公园从以罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee to another name.
sentences.zh: 李的名字命名更改为另一个名字。

sentences.en: So, Mark, then the stated reason for all of the protests and activities in Charlottesville came up in this this news conference, which was the statue of Robert E.
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，夏洛茨维尔所有抗议和活动宣称的原因，在这场新闻发布会上被提出来了，那就是位于夏洛茨维尔市中心的公园里的罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee in the park in downtown Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 李雕像。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: George Washington was a slave owner.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿是个奴隶主。

sentences.en: Was George Washington a slave owner?
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿是个奴隶主吗？

sentences.en: So will George Washington now lose his status?
sentences.zh: 那么乔治·华盛顿现在会失去他的地位吗？

sentences.en: Are we going to take down?
sentences.zh: 我们要拆除吗？

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 打扰一下。

sentences.en: Are we going to take down?
sentences.zh: 我们要拆除吗？

sentences.en: Are we going to take down statues to George Washington?
sentences.zh: 我们要拆除乔治·华盛顿的雕像吗？

sentences.en: The rather striking point that the president made here was to draw yet another equivalence.
sentences.zh: 总统在这里提出的一个相当引人注目的观点，是画出了又一个等号。

sentences.en: This was between Robert E.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee, military commander who devoted his career to breaking up the United States, and George Washington, our first president and one of the founding fathers.
sentences.zh: 李，一个把职业生涯都奉献给分裂美国的军事指挥官，与乔治·华盛顿，我们的第一任总统和开国元勋之一。

sentences.en: Trump raised the possibility or the argument that really there was very little separating George Washington from Robert E.
sentences.zh: 特朗普提出了这样一种可能性或论点，即乔治·华盛顿和罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee.
sentences.zh: 李之间其实几乎没有什么区别。

sentences.en: So if you're going to tear down a statue of a Confederate leader like Robert E.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你打算拆除像罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee, what's next?
sentences.zh: 李这样的邦联领导人的雕像，接下来是什么？

sentences.en: Tearing down a statue of George Washington or Thomas Jefferson?
sentences.zh: 拆除乔治·华盛顿或托马斯·杰斐逊的雕像？

sentences.en: How about Thomas Jefferson?
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊怎么样？

sentences.en: What do you think of Thomas Jefferson?
sentences.zh: 你觉得托马斯·杰斐逊怎么样？

sentences.en: You like him?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢他吗？

sentences.en: Okay, good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很好。

sentences.en: Are we going to take down the statue?
sentences.zh: 我们要把雕像拆了吗？

sentences.en: Because he was a major slave owner.
sentences.zh: 因为他是个主要的奴隶主。

sentences.en: Now, are we going to take down his statue?
sentences.zh: 现在，我们要拆除他的雕像吗？

sentences.en: The president pointed out that both of those founding fathers were slave owners, which is true.
sentences.zh: 总统指出，这两位开国元勋都是奴隶主，这确实是事实。

sentences.en: The difference is that George Washington and Thomas Jefferson created and laid the groundwork for the union.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，乔治·华盛顿和托马斯·杰斐逊创建并为联邦奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Robert E.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee devoted his life to tearing the union asunder.
sentences.zh: 李毕生致力于将联邦四分五裂。

sentences.en: And to sort of draw an equivalence between them was yet another startling statement on the president's part.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上将他们画上等号，是总统又一次令人震惊的言论。

sentences.en: What I assumed he was doing there was giving the protesters more of a valid reason for what they were doing,
sentences.zh: 我当时认为他这么做，是在为抗议者的行为提供一个更合理的理由，

sentences.en: one that wasn't rooted in racism or anti-Semitism or something objectionable.
sentences.zh: 一个并非根植于种族主义、反犹太主义或其他令人反感的事物的理由。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think he was trying to give them a rationale.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是在试图给他们一个合理解释。

sentences.en: There were people in that rally, and I looked the night before, if you look, there were people protesting very quietly the taking down of the statue of Robert E.
sentences.zh: 那场集会里有人，我前一天晚上看过，如果你去看看，有人非常平静地抗议拆除罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee.
sentences.zh: 李的雕像。

sentences.en: I'm sure in that group there were some bad ones.
sentences.zh: 我确信那个群体里有一些坏蛋。

sentences.en: The following day it looked like they had some rough, bad people, neo-Nazis, white nationalists, whatever you want to call them.
sentences.zh: 第二天看起来他们有一些粗暴的坏人，新纳粹分子、白人至上主义者，随你怎么称呼他们。

sentences.en: But you had a lot of people in that group that were there to innocently protest and very legally protest because, you know, I don't know if you know, they had a permit.
sentences.zh: 但那个群体里有很多人去那里进行无辜的抗议，非常合法地抗议，因为，你知道的，我不知道你知不知道，他们有许可证。

sentences.en: The other group didn't have a permit.
sentences.zh: 另一个群体没有许可证。

sentences.en: So I only tell you this.
sentences.zh: 所以我只告诉你这些。

sentences.en: There are two sides to a story.
sentences.zh: 事情都有两面性。

sentences.en: And trying to suggest that, look, this wasn't merely about wading into a crowd with clubs and mace and beating people up, that there was there was a rationale here.
sentences.zh: 试图暗示，看，这不仅仅是拿着棍棒和催泪喷雾冲进人群并殴打他人，这里面是有情理的。

sentences.en: And, by the way, it's a rationale that serious people can debate.
sentences.zh: 而且，顺便说一句，这是一个严肃的人们可以辩论的情理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You seem to be making the point that there are plenty of good Americans who think that political correctness has gone too far.
sentences.zh: 你似乎在指出，有许多优秀的美国人认为政治正确已经太过火了。

sentences.en: Yes, and that's, of course, been one of his recurring messages, and it was one of the appeals of his campaign, that he wasn't going to be held hostage to political correctness.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，这也是他反复出现的讯息之一，也是他竞选时的诉求之一，即他不会被政治正确绑架。

sentences.en: He was going to call it like he saw it.
sentences.zh: 他会实话实说。

sentences.en: The Donald Trump of this news conference was the Donald Trump of the 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 这次新闻发布会上的唐纳德·特朗普就是2016年竞选时的唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And I think it's no accident that this news conference took place in the lobby of Trump Tower,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这次新闻发布会发生在特朗普大厦的大堂里绝非巧合，

sentences.en: the same place where you remember Donald Trump came riding down that escalator to declare his candidacy.
sentences.zh: 也就是你记得唐纳德·特朗普坐着自动扶梯下来宣布参选的同一个地方。

sentences.en: For Donald Trump, the return to New York, I think, felt emotionally like the return to the candidacy, to the political pugilist,
sentences.zh: 对唐纳德·特朗普来说，回到纽约，在情感上感觉就像回到了参选的时候，回到了那个政治斗士，

sentences.en: the fighter that Donald Trump reveled in being during the campaign.
sentences.zh: 回到唐纳德·特朗普在竞选期间乐于成为的那个斗士。

sentences.en: I think that what's been difficult and perhaps not altogether happy for Donald Trump is adjusting to life in the marble mausoleum of the White House.
sentences.zh: 我认为对唐纳德·特朗普来说，一直以来艰难且或许并不那么愉快的是适应白宫大理石陵墓般的生活。

sentences.en: He's never felt fully comfortable there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里从未感到完全舒适。

sentences.en: He did feel very comfortable and seemed to be savoring the experience of being back home and giving voice to a side of Donald Trump that we do see from time to time,
sentences.zh: 他确实感到非常舒适，并且似乎在享受回家的体验，并表达出唐纳德·特朗普有时我们会看到的一面，

sentences.en: but that we haven't really seen this vividly since the election.
sentences.zh: 但自从大选以来，我们还没有真正如此生动地见过这一面。

sentences.en: So that's why it was shocking as a president, but familiar as a political candidate.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么作为总统它令人震惊，但作为政治候选人却又似曾相识。

sentences.en: Thank you all very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Do you plan to go to Charlottesville, Mr. President?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，您打算去夏洛茨维尔吗？

sentences.en: I own a house in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 我在夏洛茨维尔有一栋房子。

sentences.en: Does anyone know I own a house in Charlottesville?
sentences.zh: 有人知道我在夏洛茨维尔有一栋房子吗？

sentences.en: Oh, boy, it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，这将会是……

sentences.en: It's in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 它在夏洛茨维尔。

sentences.en: You'll see.
sentences.zh: 你会看到的。

sentences.en: Is it near the winery or something?
sentences.zh: 它是在酒庄附近还是什么地方？

sentences.en: It is the winery.
sentences.zh: 它就是那个酒庄。

sentences.en: I mean, I know a lot about Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对夏洛茨维尔了解很多。

sentences.en: Charlottesville is a great place that's been very badly hurt over the last couple of days.
sentences.zh: 夏洛茨维尔是一个好地方，在过去几天里受到了非常严重的伤害。

sentences.en: But I own actually one of the largest wineries in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但实际上我拥有美国最大的酒庄之一。

sentences.en: It's in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 它在夏洛茨维尔。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Michael.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Well, I really think jobs can have a big impact.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我真的认为工作岗位能产生重大影响。

sentences.en: I think if we continue to...
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们继续……

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, Republican leaders expressed outrage over President Trump's comments.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上，共和党领袖对特朗普总统的言论表示愤怒。

sentences.en: In a statement, House Speaker Paul Ryan said, quote,
sentences.zh: 众议院议长保罗·瑞安在声明中表示，引述：

sentences.en: We must be clear.
sentences.zh: 我们必须明确。

sentences.en: White supremacy is repulsive.
sentences.zh: 白人至上主义是令人厌恶的。

sentences.en: This bigotry is counter to all this country stands for.
sentences.zh: 这种盲目偏执违背了这个国家所代表的一切。

sentences.en: There can be no moral ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 绝不能有道德上的模棱两可。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: If you look at some of those people that you're talking about, they're outside of the country.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看你谈论的那些人，他们都在国外。

sentences.en: During his press conference at Trump Tower, the president hit back at the executives on his manufacturing council,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普大厦的新闻发布会上，总统回击了其制造业委员会的高管们，

sentences.en: who have resigned in protest of his response to the violence in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 他们为了抗议他对夏洛茨维尔暴力事件的回应而辞职。

sentences.en: They're having a lot of their product made outside.
sentences.zh: 他们的许多产品都是在外面制造的。

sentences.en: If you look at Merck as an example, take a look where, excuse me, take a look at where their product is made.
sentences.zh: 如果你以默克公司为例，看看，对不起，看看他们的产品是在哪里制造的。

sentences.en: It's made outside of our country.
sentences.zh: 它是在我们国家外面制造的。

sentences.en: We want products made in the country.
sentences.zh: 我们想要在国内制造的产品。

sentences.en: The president suggested that the reason the executives were resigning is because they do their manufacturing in other countries.
sentences.zh: 总统暗示，高管们辞职的原因是他们在其他国家进行制造。

sentences.en: They're leaving out of embarrassment because they make their products outside.
sentences.zh: 他们因为在外部制造产品而感到尴尬而离职。

sentences.en: He also addressed criticism from the CEO of Walmart, Doug McMillan, who said that the president had, quote, missed a critical opportunity to help bring our country together.
sentences.zh: 他还回应了沃尔玛首席执行官道格·麦克米伦的批评，后者曾表示总统，引述，“错过了一个帮助凝聚我们国家的关键机会”。

sentences.en: So the head of Walmart, who I know, who's a very nice guy, was making a political statement.
sentences.zh: 所以沃尔玛的负责人，我认识，他是个非常好的人，当时在发表政治声明。

sentences.en: Following the news conference, several more members of the president's manufacturing council resigned.
sentences.zh: 新闻发布会后，总统制造业委员会的几位成员又辞职了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日简报》节目到此结束。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Marlboro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·马尔伯勒。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《割草机秀》节目中，我们正为筹备假日招待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是黑灯瞎火才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会为了睡觉而昏过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何收听平台上寻找《割草机秀》。
